head: 660178ff1a881e4482b7a3cde02b51dc50cf2603
body:
Internal implementation evidence and unpublished ADR edits previously triggered the full Pages pipeline because the workflow matched `docs/**`. This PR limits both push and pull-request triggers to staged public sources and their build inputs. It preserves the publication allowlist, full Mermaid rendering, MkDocs, safety validation, internal-link checks and isolated main-only deployment behavior.

The independent review found an inherited gap in the input list: `schema_viz.py --check` executes SQLite predicate registration and domain helpers which did not trigger Pages when edited. Commit `fbf3c37` adds those ten exact Python paths and a separate-process regression that observes the real schema checker's imported repository modules and checks both trigger lists. No P7 changes are included.

Public inputs remain `docs/site/**`, `docs/schema/**`, ADR 0001/0002 and `overrides/**`, plus the builder, Schema 21 resources/configuration and executable schema-check dependencies. Internal implementation/audit/evidence documents, later ADRs and the opt-in P1–P7 DDL remain outside publication. Repository hyperlinks do not copy their targets into the site. Build commit/tree metadata identifies the last built revision, so an internal-only commit intentionally leaves that metadata unchanged.

Validation of feature HEAD `fbf3c37f6de3522e800a8cc282a332b3fbd1a0fd`, tree `21d24e4f3460b1ddbbbaf6cfa8cbd23af7020982`:

- [Pages run 38917873071](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/actions/runs/38917873071): passed. Actual downloaded job logs show ten real Mermaid SVG renders, MkDocs success, zero publication-safety violations, zero broken internal links and **8 tests passed in 1.61s**. Checkout `b3e8d39742c669b6a9d3b85d9b8156f3613999da` is the PR test merge; its effective tree equals the feature tree. Deploy was skipped; no site was deliberately deployed.
- [Development run 38917873031](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/actions/runs/38917873031): passed selected development checks; its runtime pytest execution count is zero. This is not full application acceptance.
- Independent local run on the committed feature HEAD: **8 documentation tests passed**, with JUnit and per-node journal retained; full Ruff lint and format checks passed. The schema check confirms default Core 21 / Operational 1 / Search 1.
- Local full real-render attempts failed on this managed environment: missing pinned headless Chrome; its browser download failed; the available system Chromium rejected Mermaid's local file URL under administrator policy. These failures are retained, not reported as product successes. An explicitly `--no-mermaid` local build passed MkDocs, endpoint, safety and link validation using placeholder SVGs. Real rendering is established by the exact-tree hosted run above.
- The preview artifact was uploaded, but independent artifact download returned Forbidden. Job-log ZIP retrieval succeeded and supplied the actual execution evidence.

Observed historical timings, not a controlled benchmark: the pre-skip run [38882486789](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/actions/runs/38882486789) took 21.54s for the seven documentation tests and 84s for the Pages job; [38897854723](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/actions/runs/38897854723) took 0.68s for those seven tests and 53s for its job. Both retained real full-build rendering. The final eight-test job took 68s. Path-filter avoided-run savings are expected, not directly measured by these runs; no percentage or fixed per-commit saving is claimed.

Ruleset listing returned an empty list. The branch-protection endpoint returned HTTP 403 with current credentials, so required-check configuration could not be independently established. GitHub path-filtered workflows can leave a required check pending if the owner configures one: the owner must retain an appropriate required-check policy when reviewing merge authorization. No branch protection was changed or bypassed.

Ready for separate owner merge review, subject to the owner's merge authorization and required-check policy. No merge, release, tag or Pages deployment was performed.

Evidence-only follow-up HEAD: `660178ff1a881e4482b7a3cde02b51dc50cf2603`. [Committed independent evidence](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/blob/660178ff1a881e4482b7a3cde02b51dc50cf2603/docs/implementation/evidence/pages-ci/2026-10-16-independent-review/REPORT.md) includes JUnit, per-node journal, real hosted log excerpts and SHA-256 manifests. All 74 declared publication/build inputs are byte-identical to tested `fbf3c37`; aggregate manifest digest `9693ccaccedaab3817151d43dd7ee670cf5e9b803ac6f0d341d2b5af7c22b763`. The follow-up changes only internal evidence; no full build rerun is claimed. Git metadata would identify the newer revision if rebuilt.

Subsequent actual hosted verification also completed on evidence HEAD `660178f`: [Pages38918703718](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/actions/runs/38918703718) and [Development38918703695](https://github.com/TakashiSasaki/git-repo-db/actions/runs/38918703695) passed; deploy skipped. PR path filtering uses the cumulative PR diff, so an evidence-only follow-up within this already site-changing PR still triggered Pages. Do not interpret the optimization as suppressing such synchronize runs. The new real hosted log identifies tree `ed80623514a5e574d1e24e908b95504f60b815db`; retained publication inputs remain byte-identical.
